problem: Find the disjoint union of the sets ${A}_{1}={3,\pi ,4}$ and ${A}_{2}={-1,4}.$
worked_solution:
Notice that the sets are overlapping since

$$
{3,\pi ,4}\cap {-1,4}={4}\ne ∅.
$$

So, for each of our sets, we form the associated set, where each element is tagged with the corresponding index, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & {A}_{1} &  & \,\to \, &  & {A}_{1}^{∗}={(3,1),(\pi ,1),(4,1)} \\  & {A}_{2} &  & \,\to \, &  & {A}_{2}^{∗}={(-1,2),(4,2)}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the disjoint union of our sets is simply the union of the associated tagged sets:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1}⊔{A}_{2} & ={3,\pi ,4}⊔{-1,4} \\  & ={A}_{1}^{∗}\cup {A}_{2}^{∗} \\  & ={(3,1),(\pi ,1),(4,1)}\cup {(-1,2),(4,2)} \\  & ={(3,1),(\pi ,1),(4,1),(-1,2),(4,2)}\end{aligned}
$$
